messages:
jess_support: FYI customer reported they signed up a few mins ago, applied a promo at signup, saw a success toast but no free-trial credits in billing UI. Account email is alex@acme-corp.com (customer quoted). They used Apple Pay as PM. Can billing confirm if any gating happened? :thinking:

maya_billing: Pulling the account now — acct_01GkLZ9Q. Quick check shows promo code 'WELCOME100' reached promo.apply but credits not attached. I see a flag on the profile: org_type=business (inferred from corporate domain). Looks like our promo policy disallows auto-grant for corporate domains pending manual review. Will paste log.

billing-bot: promo.apply event: {"acct":"acct_01GkLZ9Q","promo":"WELCOME100","status":"pending_manual_review","reason":"corporate_domain_detected"}

jess_support: Ugh — customer said they used personal account but company email. They insist it's for personal side-project. Customer unhappy, asking for expedited grant. Can we verify policy and manual override?

maya_billing: Policy: auto-grant only for consumer domains or emails that don't map to orgs in our risk list. Manual review required for domains on our business list or domains with >5 signups in last 30d. acme-corp.com is on the list. I can approve manually if we confirm it's not a company-paid seat. Need a short attestation from the customer or internal approval.

Devon (via DM to maya): one more data point — Apple Pay signups sometimes omit payment_method_id in our webhook payload, which makes downstream promo coupling fail because our post-signup job expects pm_id != null. If pm_id is missing AND domain is corporate, code path does pending_manual_review. Could be two independent gates.

devon_eng: Repro steps I used locally:
```
# reproduce apple-pay variant
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/signup -d '{"email":"alice@acme-corp.com","payment_source":"apple_pay","promo_code":"WELCOME100"}'
# check pubsub: signup.completed -> promo.assign
```
Result: promo.assign -> pending_manual_review when pm_id missing and domain in business list.

jess_support: Thanks Devon. For customer-facing next steps: I asked Alex (customer) to reply here with a short attestation that this is a personal account and not company-paid. Also asked for a screenshot of the Apple Pay payment success. Will paste when they send.

Alex (customer): confirmed — this is my personal side-project email but I used my company email by habit. I confirm no corporate billing, happy to sign an attestation. Screenshot: https://files.redwood.ai/attachments/attestation-123.png

maya_billing: Got attestation. I'll manually apply trial credits and note reason: 'manual override - user attestation, apple pay missing pm_id, corporate domain false positive'. Granting 1000 free tokens and 30-day trial.

billing-bot: promo.manual_grant: {"acct":"acct_01GkLZ9Q","granted_tokens":"1000","trial_days":30,"admin":"maya_billing","note":"override - attestation"}

jess_support: Confirmed with Alex — credits showed up and they can call the API now. Customer very grateful. I filed a small engineering bug for the Apple Pay pm_id path and domain false positives: BUG-9873. Tagging @devon_eng for follow-up. :thumbsup:

devon_eng: I'll pick up BUG-9873. Short-term suggestion: if pm_id missing but promo_code present and attestation provided, support can manual_grant. Long-term we'll patch the signup pipeline to not conflate pm_id absence with risk.

maya_billing: Closing this manual review. Leaving notes in billing audit and customer record. If any anomalies later ping me.

jess_support: closing thread — customer notified and satisfied. :white_check_mark:
